The existing PRUNE arms all answer the collar width question with a densifying refill, so this session fixes the refill's spacing instead.
treatment: Remove every R0 dot at d_catalogue <= collar_px. Refill (or not) from the union of the H19-5, H19-4 and H16-1 ridge supports outside the collar, admitting only cells >= spacing_px from every surviving dot and disabling every cell within spacing_px of each chosen refill, ranked by exact iterative expected-DTI gain on the fixed four-line physical field.
refill_ranking_basis: Exact iterative marginal expected-DTI gain (vendor/gems57/metric.py) among only those refill cells that keep a >= spacing_px separation from every surviving parent dot and from every already-chosen refill; candidate pool is the union of the H19-5, H19-4 and H16-1 ridge supports outside the collar; one fixed label-free physical field for all arms; no isolated-pixel shortcut and no random tie score

variants.hypothesis: The 2-3 px collar dots are net-negative: they sit on potential-field side-lobes of already-mapped traces, so they add mass S and catalogue disagreement |G| faster than they add new-fault credit T. Removing them without replacement should therefore score above R0 even though the file is 5.8% lighter.

Holding N=37,654 while replacing the collar dots with refills that are >= 3.5 px (350 m) from every other dot keeps each refill non-redundant on the 3 px kernel, so it earns full line credit instead of the 0.04-0.07 TP/dot a densified refill forfeits; this should beat R1 = PRUNEp3px (MODEL +0.005), whose refill min NN is 1.0 px.

A 400 m collar removes 1.8x more parent dots; if the existing p3.7px (-0.005) and p4.3px (-0.013) decline was caused by their densifying refill and not by losing real splays, the same collar with a spaced refill should recover to roughly break-even or slightly positive.
